newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Volcker commission settles legal issues for probe.
newsitem.headline: Volcker commission settles legal issues for probe.

text.p: Auditors for an independent committee hunting unclaimed bank accounts left behind by Nazi victims have sorted out liability issues related to the probe, a Swiss Bankers Association spokesman said on Friday.
"We have heard that a solution has been found and contracts have been agreed," the association spokeswoman Silvia Matile said.

The accountants chosen by the commission raised liability questions, but the problems have been solved, she said, noting that any further details on the arrangements would have to come directly from the commission.

Matile also said details will be released in Israel next week by the commission, headed by former U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker, on major decisions affecting its probe into the unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims still in Swiss banks.
"It is true that a public statement will be made next week ...As soon as I know when and exactly how I will make it public as usual," the spokeswoman added.

Sources close to the commission said in New York on Thursday that the body, set up last year by the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO) and Swiss banks, is expected to name the first banks to have their records audited in a pilot study that will precede an investigative audit of virtually every bank in Switzerland.
The first banks to be audited will include some of Switzerland's biggest, along with regional ones, the sources said.
They added that the commission will also discuss plans for a quasi-judicial procedure to resolve and accept claims for discovered dormant accounts in Swiss banks.
Jewish groups charge that millions -- perhaps billions of dollars -- are lying unclaimed in Swiss banks from Jews who sought a safehaven for their funds during the Second World War.
